chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from Abu al-Rabii al-Shami said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) used to say: 'When an orchard containing date palms and trees is sold for one year, it should not be sold until its fruit ripens. And when it is sold for two or three years, there is no harm in selling it after there is some greenery in it.'

key_terms.اَلْحَائِطُ: Orchard or enclosed garden with trees
key_terms.اَلْخُضْرَةُ: Greenery (vegetation not yet fully ripe or harvested)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for selling an orchard in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), transmitted via the reliable chain of al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, establishes a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence regarding the sale of fruit-bearing trees (bay' al-thimar). It distinguishes between short-term sales (one year), which require waiting for full ripeness to avoid uncertainty (gharar), and longer-term sales (two or three years), where the presence of greenery suffices as a sign of viability. This ruling reflects the Imams' practical approach to balancing market fluidity with consumer protection in agricultural transactions.
